Attack vectors: Forged 1090 MHz transmissions; capture-and-rebroadcast via SDR
Vulnerabilities: Unauthenticated, unencrypted ADS-B broadcast; no message integrity
Potential damage: Ghost aircraft injected; false / replayed position reports enter the sensing pipeline
Threat scenario: Forged 1090 MHz messages create a ghost track that the E-MLAT cross-check must reject
References as published: Costin & Francillon, Ghost in the Air(Traffic) (Black Hat, 2012); Strohmeier et al., On the Security of the ADS-B Protocol (IEEE Comms Surveys, 2017); Schafer et al., Experimental Analysis of ADS-B (2013)
Reference status: Costin, Schafer: in atlas (#59, #3). Strohmeier: published in IEEE COMST 2015, not 2017 (atlas #23).

Attack vectors: Crafted RF injection; controlled frequency offset; multipath / array spoofing
Vulnerabilities: Single-source measurement extraction; no per-measurement authentication
Potential damage: Corrupted TOA/FOA/AOA observables bias the E-MLAT localisation at source
Threat scenario: Injected frequency offset biases the FOA component of the multilateration solution
References as published: Leonardi et al., GNSS-Independent Localisation via Space-Based E-MLAT (2026); SATERA D6.1 (SESAR, 2025); Chen et al., Secure Localisation Attacks (2007)
Reference status: Leonardi 2026 and SATERA D6.1: paper sources. "Chen et al. (2007)": not located; verify or replace.

Attack types: Timing / Synchronisation manipulation, Denial of Service
Attack vectors: Delay injection; oscillator manipulation; time-source spoofing
Vulnerabilities: Sub-nanosecond synchronisation requirement; no secure time verification
Potential damage: Coherent, stealthy position error across the constellation; cross-cutting corruption of L1-L3
Threat scenario: A nanosecond-scale clock offset produces a smooth, self-consistent localisation error that anomaly detection cannot flag
References as published: Anderson et al., Secure Synchronisation for GNSS-Independent Clocks (2025); Capkun & Hubaux, Secure Positioning (2005); SATERA D6.1 (SESAR, 2025)
Reference status: "Anderson et al. (2025)": not located by web search on 20 Oct 2026. Capkun & Hubaux: real, not in atlas. Verify.

Attack vectors: Pre-deployment firmware tampering; component substitution; exposed maintenance interfaces
Vulnerabilities: COTS components; multi-vendor sourcing; no in-orbit physical inspection
Potential damage: Latent backdoor or weakened crypto activated in orbit; sensing payload compromise
Threat scenario: Backdoored receiver firmware distributed through a compromised vendor affects many satellites identically
References as published: Yu et al., Practical Exploitation of Operational Satellite Modems (2024); MITRE ATT&CK / SPARTA (2023); ASD Securing Space guidance (2026)
Reference status: "Yu et al. (2024)": title not matched (a Yu et al. 2024 CCS paper on VSAT modems exists; verify). ASD Securing Space and MITRE/SPARTA: real.

Attack vectors: External RF interference; counterfeit GNSS signals
Vulnerabilities: Aircraft self-report depends on GNSS; the integrity check itself rests on one ADS-B input
Potential damage: Denied or falsified GNSS position; the contingency the GNSS-independent layer exists to detect
Threat scenario: GNSS spoofing biases the ADS-B report; if E-MLAT is also degraded, the integrity check is defeated
References as published: Tibaldo et al., GNSS Vulnerabilities Review (2025); Wu et al., Security and Privacy of ADS-B (2020); Costin & Francillon (2012)
Reference status: Tibaldo 2025 is "GNSS-WASP: GNSS Wide Area SPoofing" (atlas #11), an attack paper, not a review. "Wu et al. 2020": title imprecise (IEEE Access 2020 ADS-B survey). Verify.

Attack vectors: Interception and modification of inter-satellite traffic; node impersonation
Vulnerabilities: Unauthenticated relay; CPS treats incoming reports as trusted
Potential damage: Altered measurements, timing metadata or ephemeris bias fusion without CPS visibility
Threat scenario: An impersonated node injects fabricated measurement reports that the CPS fuses as genuine
References as published: Salim et al., STRIDE Taxonomy for LEO Segments (2025); Yu et al. (2024); ASD Securing Space (2026)
Reference status: "Salim et al. (2025)": not located. Yu 2024: see SC-4. ASD: real.

Attack vectors: Link disruption; congestion; selective packet dropping
Vulnerabilities: Availability fluctuates with constellation geometry; no guaranteed relay redundancy
Potential damage: Degraded measurement geometry inflates DOP and position uncertainty for a targeted aircraft
Threat scenario: Selectively dropping reports from specific satellites worsens geometry without an obvious outage
References as published: Salim et al. (2025); Beidas et al., Distributed LEO Swarm Communication (2026); SATERA D6.1 (SESAR, 2025)
Reference status: "Salim (2025)", "Beidas et al. (2026)": not located. SATERA D6.1: paper source.

Vulnerabilities: Confidentiality not enforced on relay/downlink; observable relay patterns
Potential damage: Disclosure of aggregated tracks, identity associations, sensitive-aircraft movements
Threat scenario: Passive interception reveals movements of state or sensitive aircraft and enables targeting
References as published: Salim et al. (2025); Verma, Multi-Domain SATCOM Cybersecurity (2025)
Reference status: "Salim (2025)", "Verma (2025)": not located. Better evidence in atlas: #2, #63 (E3).

Attack vectors: Modification of report fields; deliberate delay of reports
Vulnerabilities: Reports carry timing metadata and ephemeris consumed without re-validation
Potential damage: Corrupted or delayed reports propagate errors into localisation and integrity monitoring
Threat scenario: Delaying selected reports distorts the TDoA solution while each message appears valid
References as published: SATERA D6.1 (SESAR, 2025); Moser et al., Cyber-Physical Attack Modelling (2016); MITRE T1565 Data Manipulation (2024)
Reference status: Moser et al. 2016 is "Investigation of Multi-device Location Spoofing Attacks on ATC" (atlas #5); the quoted title does not match. T1565 real.

Vulnerabilities: Single fusion node; downstream of all sensing-layer defences
Potential damage: Arbitrary shaping of the surveillance picture while outputs appear validated
Threat scenario: A compromised CPS process biases the multilateration solution and the track database directly
References as published: Moser et al. (2016); Salim et al. (2025); SATERA D6.1 (SESAR, 2025)
Reference status: Moser 2016: title mismatch (see SC-9). "Salim (2025)": not located.

Attack vectors: Manipulation of measurement-association or filtering logic
Vulnerabilities: Complex estimation logic; association decisions trusted
Potential damage: Mis-association or biased filtering corrupts tracks regardless of input integrity
Threat scenario: Poisoned association logic merges measurements from different aircraft into one corrupted track
References as published: Sheyner et al., Attack Graphs (2002); Adepu & Mathur, CPS Attack Analysis (2018); SATERA D6.1 (2025)
Reference status: Sheyner 2002 real (attack-graph generation); "Adepu & Mathur 2018": title generic, verify.

Potential damage: Suppressed real alerts admit spoofed positions, or false alerts disrupt operations
Threat scenario: Raising the discrepancy threshold lets a spoofed ADS-B position pass the E-MLAT cross-check
References as published: SATERA D6.1 (SESAR, 2025); Moser et al. (2016); Frigault et al., Bayesian Attack Graphs (2008)
Reference status: Frigault 2008: title imprecise (Bayesian-network security metrics); verify.

Potential damage: Loss of the surveillance picture at the point of fusion, removing separation assurance
Threat scenario: A flood of crafted reports exhausts CPS resources and blanks the surveillance output
References as published: Verma (2025); Salim et al. (2025); MITRE ATT&CK (2023)

Attack vectors: Forged or altered surveillance feed to the controller working position
Vulnerabilities: Validated picture trusted by ATM; interface boundary
Potential damage: A corrupted picture reaches the controller as authoritative, degrading situational awareness
Threat scenario: A tampered feed presents a false but plausible traffic picture at the controller position
References as published: DO-326A / ED-202A Airworthiness Security Process; SATERA D6.1 (SESAR, 2025); ED-203A (EUROCAE)
Reference status: Standards: DO-326A/ED-202A and ED-203A are real; add edition/year.

Attack vectors: Malicious command uplink; replayed command sequences; weak C2 authentication
Potential damage: Reconfiguration or disabling of defensive functions; persistent constellation-wide effect
Threat scenario: Injected commands disable on-board monitoring across multiple satellites
References as published: Yu et al. (2024); SPARTA Matrix (Aerospace Corp.); MITRE ATT&CK (2023)
Reference status: Yu 2024: see SC-4. SPARTA and ATT&CK: real; record versions (SPARTA technique list read 20 Oct 2026; ATT&CK v20).

Vulnerabilities: Constellation-wide time reference is a single trust anchor
Potential damage: Loss or corruption of the shared time base degrades all timing-dependent processing
Threat scenario: Corrupting the governed time reference induces system-wide synchronisation error
References as published: Anderson et al. (2025); SATERA D6.1 (2025); Tang et al., LEO Navigation Augmentation (2025)

Vulnerabilities: Cryptographic key and satellite-state management across a large estate
Potential damage: Key compromise enables impersonation; manipulated ephemeris biases the fusion inputs
Threat scenario: A leaked key allows an adversary to impersonate a satellite node to the CPS
References as published: ISO/IEC 27005 (2022); NIST IR 8401 Satellite Ground Segment (2022); CCSDS Space Data Link Security
